_about: Live-RLS evidence for PAIN-#5, from read-only SELECTs over pg_policies / pg_class / information_schema in project bfgglzjltfvfpobzscet. Two reads are recorded and the rows below are the later one. The 2026-10-12 read settled the question docs/SECURITY.md had hedged and answered it against the hedge: migration 006 was NOT applied, and the bridge that was live is not the policy 006 drops by name. The 2026-10-16 read is the closure: 006 was applied that day under the project owner's instruction, so `status` is PROVEN and `pgPolicies.rows` is the post-apply surface. History stays append-only in `collection[]` rather than being rewritten.
_readerWarning: The rows below are the WHOLE policy surface the catalog reports for schema `public` after migration 006 was applied on 2026-10-16: 9 policies over 7 tables. Two of them are anon-facing and both are deliberate — `telemetry` and `achievements` keep their ownerless bridge, which is the scope 006 states. Every other table carries only `Owner full access` (TO authenticated). Do not read the absence of a content-table anon row as an untested claim: tests/unit/anon-bridge-status.test.ts re-derives the expected set from supabase/migrations/*.sql and fails if the dump and the migrations disagree in either direction.
recheckBy: re-run the same SELECT any time a policy migration is applied; the bridge is closed when no row has roles={anon} on interviews, evaluations, practice_sessions, assessments or orama_index — which is what the 2026-10-16 read shows

pgPolicies.query: SELECT tablename, policyname, permissive, roles, cmd, qual FROM pg_policies WHERE schemaname = 'public' ORDER BY tablename, policyname

anonProbe.method: GET {NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/{table}?select=id&limit=5, plus ?select=id&user_id=is.null&limit=5 on the two bridge-retained tables, authenticated only with the publishable key the browser already holds. Read-only; no row content was recorded, only counts.
anonProbe.whyItCannotSettleTheQuestion: RLS filters rows, so an anon read returning [] is exactly what a closed bridge looks like AND what a table with no ownerless rows looks like. Production currently returns [] for all seven tables, so this probe is consistent with both states and proves neither.

_numbersNotOwnedHere: Expected policy counts are derived from supabase/migrations/*.sql by scripts/derive-policy-state.mjs and asserted by tests/unit/anon-bridge-status.test.ts. They are not stored in this file, so a migration edit cannot leave a stale number behind.

Statements: the pg_policies SELECT from scripts/sql/verify-anon-bridge.sql verbatim (14 rows); the closure check over the five content tables with the corrected predicate roles::text[] @> ARRAY['anon']::text[] (5 rows); per-table count(*) and count(*) FILTER (WHERE user_id IS NULL) (all seven 0/0); pg_class relrowsecurity (all seven true); information_schema.columns for the six 005 columns (all six present).
collection.identityNote: Re-read on 2026-10-16 and byte-identical to the 2026-10-12 dump: same 14 policies, same 0 rows everywhere, 005 still applied, 006 still not applied. The status therefore stays OPEN and docs/SECURITY.md's anon-bridge marker stays `open`. This pass also caught a defect in the guard rather than in the deployment: pg_policies.roles is name[], so 006's steps 2 and 3 as written raised 42883 (operator does not exist) and the migration could not run at all. Fixed here and pinned by tests/unit/sql-catalog-predicates.test.ts; the corrected closure check is what produced the 5 rows above.

collection.method: Supabase MCP, read-only except for the single authorized DDL. Statements in order: the pg_policies dump (14 rows, bridge live on all five content tables); the closure check with the corrected predicate roles::text[] @> ARRAY['anon']::text[] (5 rows); per-table count(*) and count(*) FILTER (WHERE user_id IS NULL) (all seven 0/0); pg_class relrowsecurity (all seven true); information_schema.columns for 005's six columns (all present). Then apply_migration ran 006's DO block verbatim (step 1 name drops, step 2 predicate drops, step 3 RAISE-if-survives). Then the closure check again (0 rows) and the dump again (9 rows).
collection.identityNote: 006 APPLIED 2026-10-16. The catalog went from 14 policies with `Legacy anon unowned access` on all seven tables to 9 policies with that grant retained only on telemetry and achievements — exactly the scope the migration states, and the RAISE in step 3 did not fire, so no anon grant survives on the five content tables. Status moves OPEN -> PROVEN and docs/SECURITY.md's `anon-bridge:` marker moves with it; the two are compared by this file's own gate. No row was read or written: every content table held 0 rows before and after, so the closure removed an access path, not data.

rls.whyItMatters: RLS being enabled means the anon policy is the effective gate: with it present, the publishable key alone reaches ownerless rows. Forced row security is off, which does not change that for the anon role.

rowCounts.note: count(*) and count(*) FILTER (WHERE user_id IS NULL), aggregate only — no row content read.
rowCounts.whatThisDoesToTheSeverity: No candidate data is exposed today because the project holds no rows at all. The exposure is live and permanent for writes: the anon role has ALL on the five content tables, and the app itself creates ownerless rows before sign-in (that is why 002/003 kept the bridge), so the first ownerless interview written by a visitor is readable and rewritable by anyone holding the publishable key.

columns005.conclusion: 005 IS applied — the six columns it adds are all present. The earlier note in this repo's memory that 'six columns are missing' was a point-in-time probe against a database that has since been migrated; it is superseded by this dump.

theBlindSpot: Every name-keyed check in this repo — LEGACY_BRIDGE_POLICIES, classifyBridge, and 006's own DROP list — looks for four per-operation policies ('Legacy anon select/insert/update/delete unowned'). Production has never had them: the bridge here is one policy per table named 'Legacy anon unowned access' with cmd=ALL. Fed the real dump, the repo's classifier reported 0 bridge rows where 5 exist, and applying 006 as written would DROP POLICY IF EXISTS four names that are not there and report success with the hole wide open. Detection is therefore keyed on (roles includes anon AND qual references user_id IS NULL) from this commit, not on a policy name.
